title: Succession lane deploy slate and hourly scrim notes
content:
Overview:
This is the working slate for 'succession lane' release: a stepwise traffic handoff pattern intended to replace a tight canary with a small cohort succession approach. Keeps low-latency paths in golden lane while expanding capacity across region-primary, region-fallback, and dedicated pool.

Goals:
- minimize user-facing latency blips during model switching
- provide predictable rollback points at 10/30/60/100% allocations
- capture per-hour telemetry snapshots for drift/regression detection

Quick deploy calendar (hourly cadence):
- H-3: final preflight: smoke on staging, golden-lane smoke, key metrics snapshot saved (tag: preflight-2026-12-06)
- H-1: release build pinned, infra green, ops channels staffed (owner: Lena)
- T+0 (00:00 UTC): start succession lane phase 1 -> 10% traffic to new model variant (window: 15m)
- T+1h: verify telemetry window #1 (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost delta), decision point: proceed/hold/rollback
- T+2h: increase to 30% (window: 30m)
- T+4h: telemetry window #2 -> if stable, 60%
- T+6h: final increase to 100% if all gates pass
- T+24h: post-rollout telemetry digest and preliminary retro notes

Preflight checklist (sprinty):
- [ ] Confirm model binary + checksum in storage (S3: s3://redwood-releases/2026-12/succession-v2)
- [ ] All infra jobs green (k8s nodes, GPU pool availability)
- [ ] Canary runner script updated and tested locally (script: tools/canary/succession-runner.sh)
- [ ] Alert rules in PagerDuty reflect new metric names (ops-alerts:latency-succession-v2)
- [ ] Slack deploy channel created and invited: #deploy-succession-lane
- [ ] Ensure fallback variants are registered in routing-table (route-service: tag fallback-v1)
- [ ] Confirm docs for SRE handoff are in Confluence (linked_artifacts above)

Telemetry sampling plan (per-hour snapshots):
- Capture: p50, p95 latency, errors (5xx, model-decoding exceptions), average tokens, input-length distribution, KV cache hit %, tail-latency >500ms count
- Export windows: 15m rolling plus hourly aggregated snapshot stored in monitoring-bucket (prefix: telemetry/succession/2026-12)
- Quick smoke dashboards: runbook dashboard + 'diff vs baseline' panel (baseline = last stable release)

Succession lanes (traffic policy):
- Phase 1: 10% (cohort A) — route by cookie/region-shard; if region failure, fallback to legacy variant immediate (0s)
- Phase 2: 30% (cohort B) — expand to users with high request volume but low idempotence (watch throttles)
- Phase 3: 60% (cohort C) — widen locality; enable autoscale buffer +2 nodes in dedicated pool
- Phase 4: 100% — retire legacy variant after 2h stablization

Fallback and rollback triggers (operational):
- Immediate rollback if error-rate increases > 0.5% absolute vs baseline for two consecutive 15m windows
- Hold and investigate if p95 latency regresses by > 30% vs baseline and user-facing experience reports start coming in
- Manual rollback threshold: ops lead + SRE approval required if there is any data-exfil path (edge case)

Communications matrix (who pings whom):
- Exec alert: only if full-region degradation or >1% traffic failing for >30m (owner: Head of SRE)
- Prod eng channel (#prod-eng): for roll-forward/rollback commands and roll-call
- Customer success: short heads-up 1h before 100% completion in case of enterprise customers on dedicated clusters

Release notes (draft - to be copy-edited for public changelog):
- Release: Succession-lane model variant v2 (internal id: succession-v2)
- Key changes: improved KV-cache memory utilization, attention kernel micro-optimizations for long-inputs, reduced token inflation in beam sampling path
- Expected impact: up to 12% lower per-token latency for median requests; slight increase in memory footprint on large-batch workloads (monitoring advised)
- Known limitations: multi-turn chats with >8k context may have cache-warmup spikes during first 2 requests; we recommend enabling warm-start for those sessions

Post-release followups (48h and 7-day):
- 48h: collect incident tickets opened, summarize any user-facing regressions, push hotfix backports if needed
- 7-day: run quality regression eval against internal prompt set (eval-suite: release/succession-v2) and attach to release ticket
- Retro prompts: what gating missed signal, where did ops toggle early, are unit economics aligned (cost per 1M tokens)

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Should we add a short-circuit for region-latency-only degradation (i.e., shift that region entirely to fallback variant) or keep global rule? Pros/cons listed in comments below.
- Need to confirm whether dedicated-pool +2 nodes is sufficient in eu-west-1; ask infra for capacity headroom numbers (cc: Priya)
- Quick FYI: Marco to validate PD escalation runbook entries for this path before H-1

References and links:
- Jira: RELEASE-2026 (linked above)
- PR: inference-runtime#841 (linked above)
- Slack threads: #deploys (see thread ts: 2026-11-29T15:20 UTC)

Short retrospective checklist (after postmortem):
- Archive hourly telemetry snapshots under a labeled folder with decision notes
- Update traffic policy snippets in routing-service repo based on what actually ran
- Create short 'lessons learned' blurb for weekly release-ops sync

End of slate — leave inline comments below and I will fold into a tidy runbook before finalizing.
